issues.description: Interface name mismatch: The problem statement (UML and text) defines an interface named 'Milkable' with the abstract method messageOnMilk(). In the solution repository, an interface named 'Dairy' is provided with messageOnMilk(), while solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java is empty and Seal.java and Goat.java implement 'Dairy' (not 'Milkable'). This naming inconsistency between 'Milkable' (expected by the specification/tests) and 'Dairy' (used in the solution) will confuse students and can cause mismatches when comparing student code to the reference or when tests expect the 'Milkable' identifier.

The concept is an interface representing animals that can be milked. The problem statement and UML explicitly name this interface 'Milkable' (problem_statement.md: lines 51-53). The template Main.java also refers to 'Milkable' when building the milkables array (template repository src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java: lines 22-24). The solution repository instead implements this concept using an interface named 'Dairy' (solution repository src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java), and the solution repository contains an empty file named Milkable.java (solution repository src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java) which increases the mismatch/confusion. This one-to-one identifier mismatch between 'Milkable' (problem/template) and 'Dairy' (solution) prevents a clear mapping for students: they will look for or implement 'Milkable' following the exercise and UML, while the reference implementation and implementing classes use 'Dairy', causing cognitive friction and potential build/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across all artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution interface 'Dairy' to 'Milkable' so it matches the UML/problem statement: rename Dairy.java -> Milkable.java, change the interface declaration to 'public interface Milkable' and ensure it declares String messageOnMilk(); update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement Milkable (instead of Dairy). Remove or replace the empty Milkable.java file in the solution repository so there is a single correctly named interface implementation. Alternatively, if you prefer the 'Dairy' name, update the problem statement and template to use 'Dairy' everywhere, but keep consistent naming across all artifacts.
